questions.q: There are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> men and two women participating in a chess tournament. Each participant plays two games with every other participant. If the number of games played by the men between themselves exceeds the number of games played between the men and the women by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>84</mn></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, number of men is m and number of women is 2.

Since each participants competes two games with each other, Hence count of men Vs men total number of game plays =2 mC2.

count of men Vs women total number of game plays =4m.

As per given condition in question,

2 mC2=84+4 m

⇒m2-5 m-84=0

⇒m2-12 m+7 m-84=0

⇒m-12m+7=0.

⇒m=12, -7

Now, first we will arrange letters _M_A_T_H_E_M_A_T_I_.

Here, we have 10 gaps to fill C & S.

The number of words with or without meaning can be formed from the word MATHEMATICS when C, S does not come together is

=9!2!·2!·2!×C210×2!

questions.q: The number of numbers, strictly between 5000 and 10000 can be formed using the digits 1,3,5,7,9 without repetition, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Numbers 1,3,5,7,9

Now to form number between 5000-10000

_⏟5,7,9_⏟4 ways_⏟3 ways_⏟2 ways

Here at 1000's place should be taken by 5, 7 & 9

So for 1000's place there will be 3 ways,

Now for hundredth place there will be 4 ways,

For ten's place there will be 3 ways,

And for unit place there will be 2 ways,

So total ways will be 3×4×3×2=72 ways.

questions.q: The letters of the word OUGHT are written in all possible ways and these words are arranged as in a dictionary, in a series. Then the serial number of the word TOUGH is :

questions.solution:
Lets arrange the letters of OUGHT in alphabetical order.

G,H,O,T,U

Number of words starting with G

=4!=24

Number of words starting with H

=4!=24

Number of words starting with O

=4!=24

Number of words starting with TG

3!=6!

Number of words starting with TH

=3!=6

Number of words starting with TOG

=2!=2

Number of words starting with TOH

=2!=2

Next word is TOUGH.

Hence, the serial number of the word TOUGH is

=24+24+24+6+6+2+2+1=89

questions.q: The number of ways of selecting two numbers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>b</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>99</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> is the remainder when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></math> is divided by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>23</mn></math> is

a+b=23λ+2

If λ=1, then

a+b=25

So, 1,24,3,22,....,23,2

a+b=48

No ordered pair possible.

If λ=3, then

a+b=71

So,

1,70, 3,68, 5,66,....,61,10, 63,8, 65,6, 67,4, 69,2

Total 35 ordered pairs.

If λ=5, then

a+b=117

17,100, 19,98, ..., 99,18

So,

questions.q: The number of five-digit numbers, greater than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40000</mn></math> and divisible by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math>, which can be formed using the digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>7</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn></math> without repetition, is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We need to find the number of 5 digit numbers greater than 40000 and divisible by 5.

Case I : Numbers start with 5.

Here if the number starts with 5 it should end with 0 to be divisible by 5.

Case II : Number starts with 7 and the last digit can have 0 or 5.

Case III : The number starts with 9 and the last digit should have 0 or 5.

Total numbers =120.

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.solution:

questions.q: The number of seven digits odd numbers, that can be formed using all the seven digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>5</mn></math> is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
To find the number of 7 digit odd number formed by using the seven digits 1,2,2,2,3,3,5

We will take following cases,

Case 1- fixing 1 as unit place,

So total number of ways will be 6!3!2! as 2 is repeating three times and 3 is repeating two times

Case 2- fixing 3 unit place,

So total number of ways will be 6!3!

Case 3- fixing 5 as unit place,

So total number of ways will be 6!3!2!

Now adding all the cases we will get, total number of ways as 6!3!2!+6!3!+6!3!2!=60+120+60=240

questions.q: A class contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>b</mi></math> boys and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi></math> girls. If the number of ways of selecting <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> boys and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> girls from the class is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>168</mn></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>g</mi></math> is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, b boys and g girls

Also given total ways of selecting 3 boys and 2 girls which will be C3b×C2g=168

⇒  bb-1b-26×gg-12=168

⇒  bb-1b-2gg-1=7×6×4×3×2×2

⇒   bb-1b-2gg-1=8×7×6×3×2

Now on comparing both side we get, b=8 and g=3  ⇒b+3g=8+9=17

Number of words Arranging all the letters = 6!

questions.q: The lines L1,L2,...,L20 are distinct. For n=1,2,3,...,10 all the lines L2n−1 are parallel to each other and all the lines L2n pass through a given point P. The maximum number of points of intersection of pairs of lines from the set L1,L2,...,L20 is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

Out of 20 numbered lines, even numbered lines are concurrent, odd number lines are parallel.

So, the maximum number of intersection points will be given by,

N=1→point of intersection when both lines are even+0→point of intersection when both lines are parallel+C110×C110→point of intersection when 1 odd and 1 even line meets

⇒N=1+0+100

⇒N=101

questions.q: The number of words, with or without meaning, that can be formed by taking 4 letters at a time from the letters of the word 'SYLLABUS' such that two letters are distinct and two letters are alike, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
From the given word, S-2,L-2,A,B,Y,U.

Number of alike letter pairs =2

Number of ways to select one pair=C12

Number of distinct letters=5

Number of ways to select two distinct letters=C25

Number of ways to arrange four letters if two are alike=4!2!

Required number of ways =C12C25·4!2!=2·10·242=240
